newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss money market steady, SNB not aggressive.
newsitem.headline: Swiss money market steady, SNB not aggressive.

text.p: Swiss money market rates were steady in early trading as the Swiss National Bank (SNB) placed funds but at market rates, dealers said.
Tom/next was quoted at around 1.81/2.06 percent, and dealers said they expected rates around two percent to prevail.
The SNB said last week it was continuing to add liquidity to the market after several other European central banks, including the Bundesbank, moved to lower money market rates.
But its activity today was normal.
"The National Bank has not done anything special. They are placing funds but at market rates," one dealer said.
The market was turning its attention to the month's end to see whether the central bank would inject enough liquidity to keep rates steady a time demand usually climbs.
"It will be important to see what happens at the end of the month," one dealer said. "I hope there will not be any tension."

He said a smooth transition into September would mean the SNB had achieved its goal of pushing short-term rates lower. If liquidity is squeezed, rates would quickly climb to around three percent, he added.
